title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 136
paragraphs: That was their answer to Hydarnes. When they had gone up to Susa and come into the king's presence, the spear-bearers of the guard first ordered them, and tried to compel them by force, to do obeisance to the king by prostrating themselves. They said they would do no such thing, even if the guards pushed them down head-first, for it was not their custom to do obeisance to a man, and they had not come there for that purpose. After resisting this, they spoke words to this effect: “O king of the Medes, the Lacedaemonians have sent us in place of the heralds killed at Sparta, to pay the penalty for their lives.” At this, Xerxes, moved by a spirit of magnanimity, replied that he would not be like the Lacedaemonians, who had violated the customs accepted by all men by killing heralds; he would not do himself what he blamed them for doing, nor would he free the Lacedaemonians from their guilt by killing these men in return.
